children: The National Stock Exchange of India Ltd's (NSEI.NS) $2.3 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed on the second day of bidding, driven by strong demand from institutional investors.
The IPO received bids for about 88.3 million shares, against 88.6 million on offer, as of 2:44 p.m. IST on Friday, exchange data showed.

The $2.3 billion IPO is one of India's largest ever and comes in a period when the primary market is drawing major issuers, including billionaire Mukesh Ambani-backed Jio Platforms, which is expected to list by year-end. NSE's float would crown a decade-long effort, in which regulatory scrutiny and legacy legal issues repeatedly delayed its listing.
Up to half of the IPO is reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), including anchor investors, while about 35% of the shares are set aside for retail investors.

The stock exchange operator on Wednesday allotted shares worth $703.04 million to marquee global and domestic investors, including the sovereign wealth funds of Norway and Abu Dhabi, as part of its anchor book allocation ahead of the IPO. LIC was the top investor in the anchor book.
The IPO is entirely an offer for sale by existing shareholders, with NSE receiving no proceeds. The public issue closes on Monday, with shares expected to begin trading from September 24.
